texts: good. the arrival, Eli's apprentice typing and name, and the date all land. One caveat no rewording fixes: "day 455 of Year 2" is stored as Day 455 plus Year 2, with nothing marking it as a day-of-year rather than a day-of-month.
good. the coming is recorded with the Keeper family as its source, and keeper_family is linked to family.
good. the assignment carries the Council as agent, Eli as theme and Norren as recipient.

bad: the parse records only that Norren was part of the Council and never types him with the clause's own predicate noun, so "was Norren a member?" finds nothing — half of what the sentence says is dropped. Spell the head noun out as the predicate so the typing cannot be missed: "Norren was a member of the Council."

mixed: the denial itself is right — no apprentice-taking by Norren, with the indefinite apprentice kept inside it — but the bare "before" is dropped, because a bare sequence adverb has no slot, so nothing records that this is prior to Eli's arrival. Give the anteriority an explicit anchor: "Norren had not taken an apprentice before the Council assigned Eli to him."

good. the case is typed and linked to Norren by possession, leather_case is linked to case, and the carrying's start is anchored on her second night. (That boundary points at the night entity rather than a calendar term — a recorded limitation, not lost content.)

mixed: the denial and its scope are right — the solo-tending and the indefinite lantern both stay inside it — and "during" is the frame word the instruction set actually licenses, but the six-month period comes out with no kind at all (its only class atom is the property "first"), so nothing says what that period is. Your wording already supplies the head noun ("months"), so no rewrite would help here; the repair is translator-side — type the span as six months.

bad: the "of" joining the nightly supervision to the six-month span is rendered with the During head, which is reserved for during/while/throughout — and the compliant alternative has no carrier for a bounding span at all, so the six-month limit would vanish and the sentence would read as supervision every night without end. Use the word that is licensed, exactly as the previous sentence does: "Norren supervised Eli every night during her first six months."
